trust_decision.summary: Whether a request-supplied xsd:anyURI DSML value is fetched server-side is decided in ByteStringUtility.convertValue's URI branch, which at the pinned commit unconditionally calls URI.toURL().openStream(); the fixed version moves that decision into convertUri behind a static flag set from servlet context-params in DSMLServlet.init, while web.xml separately decides whether the gateway requires container authentication at all.

landing_point.why: It is the only server-side fetch of a request-supplied URI in the tree (URI.toURL().openStream()), it is reached from every DSML operation, and the advisory's SSRF, local-file-read and unbounded-read all resolve to this one call.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP POST /DSMLServlet, dsml batchRequest values: add (DSMLAddOperation.java:93), modify (DSMLModifyOperation.java:107), compare (DSMLCompareOperation.java:84), search filter/substring (DSMLSearchOperation.java:114,133,152,174,194,285,295,298), extended requestValue (DSMLExtendedOperation.java:104)
HTTP /DSMLServlet route via container-managed BASIC authentication (security-constraint added at the servlet mapping)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: None applies: every DSML operation funnels through the one convertValue branch, so hardening it covers every route; the nearest dismissible-looking surface is the web.xml auth requirement, which a solver could wave off as 'container configuration, not application code'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: DSML clients may legitimately send xsd:anyURI-typed attribute values in add/modify/compare/search requests; with dereferencing disabled the value must still be accepted and stored as its literal URI string, so a fix that rejects all URI values (or applies the scheme/host allowlist to values that are never fetched) breaks legitimate DSML writes and comparisons.

O6_input_shapes: single value element vs repeated value elements vs substring initial/any/final vs extended requestValue (all generated as java.lang.Object)
java.net.URI (the branch the fix changes) vs the String, byte[] and DOM Element branches in the same method
URI with a disallowed scheme (file, ftp, gopher, jar, urn) or with no scheme / relative / opaque
IPv4 host literals: loopback, 0.0.0.0/8, 169.254/16 metadata, RFC1918 site-local, multicast, 100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT, 192.0.0.0/24, 198.18.0.0/15, 240.0.0.0/4
IPv6 literals: ::1, fe80::/10 link-local, fc00::/7 unique-local
host names that resolve to zero or several addresses, and a URI with no host
HTTP 3xx redirect response vs 2xx/4xx, and response body under vs over the size cap

O7_producer.where: opendj-dsml-servlet/resources/schema/DSMLv2.xsd:137-139 (DsmlValue = union of string/base64Binary/anyURI) with opendj-dsml-servlet/resources/schema/bindings.xjb:19-70 binding the value elements to java.lang.Object, plus the JVM-wide System.setProperty("mapAnyUriToUri","true") at DSMLServlet.java:194

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Follow search-result references: fetch the anyURI ref (DSMLv2.xsd:376) returned by the LDAP server.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The handler already receives OP_TYPE_SEARCH_RESULT_REFERENCE and drops it; implementing LDAP referral chasing is the obvious next feature and would add a server-side fetch that convertUri never sees.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Reuse the existing read(url)/readProperties(url) helper from the gateway to fetch a URI.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the repo's only other URL-fetch helper, accepts any scheme with no allowlist, address or size check, and copying it into the DSML gateway to avoid duplicate code is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second deployment descriptor (or alternate container config) mapping the servlet without the security-constraint.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: sun-web.xml:1-4 already ships beside web.xml and only tweaks the class-loader; someone adding another container's descriptor could copy the servlet mapping without the auth block.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Pass request controls through and dereference a URI-valued controlValue (xsd:anyType).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: DSML controls are currently dropped by every operation; adding control passthrough is a natural feature and controlValue is untyped, so a URI there would bypass convertValue.

O9_family: SSRF / arbitrary local file read / unbounded read (CWE-918, CWE-73, CWE-400)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module reactor (parent opendj-parent 5.1.2-SNAPSHOT; maven.compiler.source/target 11, pom.xml:44-45); opendj-dsml-servlet is a WAR generated with jaxb2-maven-plugin XJC and maven-war-plugin
services: servlet container (cargo tomcat10x, pom.xml:63, for the module's integration-test phase)
OpenDJ LDAP server on localhost for end-to-end DSML requests
O10_build.project_tests: opendj-dsml-servlet has no src/test directory at the pinned commit (Glob over the module); the published fix adds ByteStringUtilityTestCase (in-memory, no network/DNS) and a commons build-tools test dependency, so this area had no tests before the fix.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a file: scheme check (or an outright reject of obj instanceof URI) in convertValue's URI branch: the first leaves http/https SSRF, internal/metadata hosts, redirects and unbounded reads open, the second breaks legitimate xsd:anyURI storage.

out_of_scope_notes: opendj-server-legacy/src/main/java/org/opends/server/config/Functions.java:70-77 has the same URI-fetch primitive (read/readProperties, any scheme, no host or size guard) but it is driven by administrator-supplied configuration expressions, not the unauthenticated DSML gateway.

opendj-core src/main/java/com/forgerock/opendj/util/ManifestUtil.java:70 and src/main/java/org/forgerock/opendj/security/OpenDJProviderSchema.java:59 open fixed classpath/manifest URLs, not request data.

Full Maven reactor build and an offline test run were not attempted (project code must not be run).

The JAXB detail that xsd:anyURI (union bound to java.lang.Object plus mapAnyUriToUri=true) yields java.net.URI rather than String was inferred from the fix's own premise and the schema/bindings, not executed.
O1 is counted as one public HTTP route (/DSMLServlet); five DSML operation handlers reach the same sink but are payload types of that single route.
Whether hidden behaviour tests exercise the web.xml container-auth change (needs a deployed servlet container) is unknown; latest-release data was 'none', so latest_where for any route is unknown.
